messages.author: f2b64d27814968e8
messages.subject: D5 MRDS
parts:
Hello

=20

I am just beginning to use the D5 MRDS engine and I must congratulate =
the developers on bringing us yet another improvement on this great =
software package.

=20

I have 2 questions:

=20

I am analyzing a series of surveys, only the last of which was done with =
double observers. For comparability, I have analyzed them all as single =
platform surveys, but it is of interest to get a g(0) estimate for the =
last survey, with an associated measure of variance. In the D5 output, =
the point estimates for p(0) are given but the variance is not =
immediately obvious to me. Is it the se of the intercept term in the =
conditional detection function? (sorry if this is an obvious question).

=20

Secondly, I am analyzing a survey that was done in Buckland-Turnock (BT) =
mode, where the secondary platform was aware of the sightings of the =
primary platform, but the primary was not aware of the sightings of the =
secondary. As I understand it the secondary only registered a sighting =
if they made it first. Therefore, if they heard the primary make a =
sighting they had not yet seen, they would not register it themselves. =
It seems to me that this survey should be analyzed in trial =
configuration because there is only one-way independence. But I was =
wondering what the ramifications would be of analyzing in independent =
observer mode? I ask this because it is of interest to get an estimate =
of g(0) for the combined platforms, which is not possible with the trial =
mode. I cannot think why the estimate of p(0) for the combined observers =
would not be valid.

=20

I appreciate any help I can get. Many thanks,

=20

messages.subject: Re: D5 MRDS
parts:
Daniel:
Q1: This was an oversight on my part in not including an se for g(0) (or=20
what we call p(0) in the output) because I had not envisioned it being=20
used as you'ld like. I'll be going through the code in the next couple=20
of weeks tidying up loose ends for a final release and will output the=20
se. In the time being you can compute it yourself if the model is=20
simple. You are on the right track but it will depend on the model you=20
used for the conditional detection function. If you have only distance=20
in the conditional det fct model then the se of the intercept is the=20
correct value to use except that you need to translate it to p(0). =20
However, if you ever other covariates which you are likely to have then=20
you won't have all the information you need to compute it. I think I'll=20
change this to ouput the v-c matrix for the parameters so any variance=20
can be computed.=20

Q2: If the data are set up as IO in the way that you described then all=20
of the trials for the secondary observer will be seen because the=20
secondary will have "seen" all the primary sightings, so the result will=20
be that p(0) for the secondary observer will be 1 so the pooled p(0)=20
will be 1, which is not what you are looking for presumably. I'm=20
somewhat guessing what you are looking for so maybe you can send a=20
message directly to me that describes the setup in more detail. If I=20
think it is useful for the list I'll cc the list as well with my=20
response. If what you want is p(0) for both teams combined assuming=20
that p(0) is the same for both teams, then it would be=20
p_both(0)=3D2*p(0)-p(0)^2

regards --jeff
